outcome_classes.description: Returns a list of tickets matching the queue and status filters (clm-api-json-007, clm-notes-md-008).
No claim describes what is returned when no ticket matches the queue/status filters (see gap-find-tickets-empty).
Not applicable as a distinct case in the claims: find_tickets is a list search, not a lookup by identifier, and no claim addresses a not-found case for it.
No claim describes what happens when queue, status, or action is given a value outside its enumerated set (see gap-invalid-enum-values).
No claim describes what happens when the required action field is omitted entirely (see gap-missing-action-field).
Returns one ticket with its comments, ordered by comment position (clm-api-json-008, clm-notes-md-009).

Not applicable as stated: get_ticket returns a single ticket, not a collection that can be legitimately empty; whether the comments list can be empty is separately unaddressed (see gap-get-ticket-zero-comments).
No claim describes what get_ticket returns when given a ticket_id that does not exist (see gap-get-ticket-not-found).
No claim describes what happens when the required action field is omitted, or when ticket_id is missing or malformed (see gap-missing-action-field).
No claim states whether comments are returned as an empty list or omitted when a ticket exists but has zero comments (see gap-get-ticket-zero-comments).

invariants.statement: comment_count on a ticket equals the number of comment records attached to it; a stored value that disagrees is overwritten on read (clm-notes-md-005, clm-notes-md-006).
ticket_id is unique across every queue (clm-notes-md-007).

queue is restricted to billing or shipping: api.json enumerates exactly these two values and notes.md independently states ticketq fronts two queues, billing and shipping (clm-api-json-004, clm-notes-md-001).
invariants.prose: queue takes only the values billing and shipping.

invariants.statement: Inferred from notes.md, not stated by any schema field: a ticket's blocker is named somewhere within the text of its comments, but no field structurally marks which comment or what text names it (clm-notes-md-010).
invariants.prose: body may name the ticket's blocker as free text; no structured field marks this.

goals.statement: Find the ticket in a given queue that still needs the engineer to act on it.
Explain why a ticket is stuck by finding the ticket, then reading its comments for the named blocker.

gaps.subject: query_tickets with a missing or invalid action value
gaps.unknown: What query_tickets returns or raises when action is omitted (though required, per clm-api-json-002) or given a value other than find_tickets/get_ticket.
gaps.why_it_matters: Neither input artifact describes any error behaviour for query_tickets; a scenario testing the required field or the two-value enum has no stated ground truth to assert against.

gaps.subject: find_tickets with no matching tickets
gaps.unknown: What find_tickets returns when no ticket matches the queue/status filters given.
gaps.why_it_matters: No claim states the empty-result shape (empty list vs. an error vs. something else), so a scenario built on the empty outcome class has no stated ground truth.

gaps.subject: get_ticket with a ticket_id no ticket has
gaps.unknown: What get_ticket returns or raises for an unknown ticket_id. No claim in this claim set addresses it, and unlike the api.json/notes.md/trace.json fixture, this run has no third artifact corroborating either an error or an empty-object behaviour -- there is nothing here to resolve, only silence.
gaps.why_it_matters: Both goals recorded here route through get_ticket; without a stated not-found behaviour neither goal's error path can be scored or instantiated soundly.

gaps.subject: queue and status given values outside their enumerated sets
gaps.unknown: Whether query_tickets errors, ignores the filter, or does something else when queue or status is given a value other than the ones api.json enumerates.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is a bad-argument path a real client can trigger, and no claim states its behaviour.

gaps.subject: get_ticket on a ticket whose comment_count is 0
gaps.unknown: Whether the comments array is present-but-empty or omitted when a ticket has no comments.
gaps.why_it_matters: A ticket that is open but not yet worked on plausibly has zero comments, and the goal-explain-why-stuck path needs a stated shape for that case to be instantiated or scored.
